subject: EdgeBurst dedicated capacity: recommended SKU mix and memory safeguard
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@edgeburst.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Rao <samira@edgeburst.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing help: Dedicated footprint for EdgeBurst ML inference

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for taking a look. Quick summary of the workload we expect to move to Dedicated:
- Primary model: community open-llm family (we'll provide model bits) quantized to 4-bit for most routes.
- Traffic mix: steady real-time chat-style traffic ~30 qps baseline, expected burst up to ~90 qps (3x) during peak events.
- Typical request: 95% short-turn completions (avg seq length ~256 tokens).
- Long-form jobs: ~3% of requests are long-generations, up to 1024 tokens, and occasionally run concurrently.
- Latency target: p95 < 120ms for short completions.
- Concurrency: sustained 300 concurrent short sessions, 20 concurrent long gens at peak.
- KV/prefix cache: average per-session KV ~1.2GB (clients want sticky chat history cached).
- Model memory footprint (in our current profiling): H100-80GB variant fits unquantized, A100-40GB variant for 16/8-bit, L4-24GB good for quantized distilled variants.

Can you recommend a practical Dedicated SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4), how much reserve we should contract for vs burst capacity, and operational notes (KV cache sizing, autoscale settings, fallback policy)? I've attached our initial workload report.

Attachment: EdgeBurst_initial_workload_report.pdf (1 file, PDF)

Thanks — Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeBurst AI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sizing help: Dedicated footprint for EdgeBurst ML inference — quick SKU analysis

Jordan / team —

Quick read of the profile and attaching a small CSV with our token/latency projections (RBW-2334_MLP_profiler.csv). High level recommendation below; I focused on hitting p95 <120ms for short completions while keeping committed spend reasonable.

Executive summary
- Recommended reserve: mix of L4 + A100, with a small H100 pool for memory-heavy long gens and cache residency.
- Why mixed: L4 provides the best cost/perf for short quantized chat (low latency, high qps), A100 gives reliable throughput for quantized mid-length requests and offline batching, H100 is necessary where you want big memory headroom and to avoid model sharding for long gens or large KV residency.

Sizing (initial reserved configuration) — conservative starting point for pilot:
- L4: 10 x L4 (24GB) reserved. Rationale: L4 handles small-seq quantized inferencing with low tail latency; 10 L4s give headroom for ~300 concurrent short sessions with aggressive continuous batching and 8-12 request batching windows.
- A100: 4 x A100 (40GB) reserved. Rationale: mid-length sequences and throughput-heavy routes; ideal for quantized 8/16-bit models where we want denser batching and better memory than L4.
- H100: 2 x H100 (80GB) reserved. Rationale: keep two large-memory nodes for model variants that require full weight residency (or for long-generation fallthrough), and for large KV caches pinned in GPU memory for the hottest sessions.

Burst/Autoscale:
- Add burst pool: 8 x L4 + 4 x A100 as burst capacity (preemptible / on-demand) to cover 3x peak traffic events. Prefer burst to be in the same region with fast routing.
- Autoscale policy: maintain min-reserved as above; scale up burst when queue depth > 50 or p95 exceeds 110ms for >60s. Scale down when p95 stable <90ms for 3 minutes.

KV / cache sizing:
- Recommend distributed KV cache across H100 and A100 nodes for residency of hot contexts. Target hot-residency ~400–600GB (not per-node) so active sessions see cache hits. If clients insist on per-session 1.2GB, prioritize LRU eviction and set max sticky history to 3–4 turns for large sessions.
- If EdgeBurst wants to support full 1.2GB per session with 300 concurrent sessions, that'll require ~360GB of fast host memory + 1–2 H100 GPUs pinned for GPU-resident KV — cost will be high. Recommend product change to soft-limit history length or offload cold history to fast SSD-backed cache (NVMe) with async prefetch.

Latency & batching recommendations:
- For p95 <120ms: keep max batching window 20ms, max batch size 12 for short routes on L4; A100 can tolerate 40ms window with larger batch sizes for throughput jobs.
- Enable prefix KV caching for short completions aggressively. Use local L4 KV for the hottest 10% of sessions.

Fallback & routing:
- Route by policy: prefer L4 for chat route, fallback to A100 if L4 capacity exhausted, finally fall back to H100 for long gen/compatibility. H100 can also be used for safe-mode when model variant mismatch occurs.

Operational notes:
- Warmup: pre-warm L4 nodes with small synthetic traffic for 5–10 minutes before day-of peak events.
- Observability: add token-level p95 metric per route and a KV-hit-rate dashboard. Alert when KV-hit-rate drops below 65% or p95 >120ms for >120s.
- Contracting: suggest reserving the L4 majority (70% of compute by piece) with a contractual burst pool for A100/H100. This keeps committed cost predictable while giving safety for long gens.

Estimated starting committed footprint (approx monthly slots):
- 10 L4 (reserved) + 4 A100 (reserved) + 2 H100 (reserved) with burst pool as above.

Attachments: RBW-2334_MLP_profiler.csv (profiling numbers and latency curves)

Happy to join a call with Tom to walk through the tradeoffs.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@edgeburst.ai>
Cc: Samira Rao <samira@edgeburst.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing help: Dedicated footprint for EdgeBurst ML inference — proposed plan

Tom —

Thanks for the profile. We digested the data and put together a concise recommended plan (attached). Short version below so you can move quickly:

Customer-facing summary (for procurement / architecture)
- Recommended committed reserve: 10 x L4 + 4 x A100 + 2 x H100.
  - L4s handle the bulk of short, quantized chat traffic (keeps p95 under target and is cost-efficient).
  - A100s act as throughput and mid-length workhorses.
  - H100s reserved for long-generation fallthrough and GPU-resident KV for the hottest sessions.
- Burst pool: 8 x L4 + 4 x A100 available for spikes (3x peak coverage).
- KV approach: hot KV pinned to H100/A100 memory (~400–600GB target hot-residency); cold history to NVMe with async prefetch.
- Autoscale trigger: queue depth and p95-based scaling; conservative cooldown windows to avoid flapping.

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- This week (by Fri): Redwood provides a one-page playbook covering routing, autoscale thresholds, and cost/latency tradeoffs (attached: EdgeBurst_dedicated_playbook_v1.docx).
- Next: technical deep-dive with your infra team — propose Wed, 2028-03-10 10:00am PT for a 60-minute session to review KV sizing and warmup strategy.
- Procurement: once sizing is agreed, we’ll provide a draft Dedicated contract with the reserved + burst configuration for signature (target 2–3 week turnaround).

Costs and options
- If EdgeBurst wants to minimize committed spend, alternative: reserve fewer A100s and lean more on burst A100s during known campaign windows. We can build a spike calendar into the autoscaler.

Attaching: EdgeBurst_dedicated_playbook_v1.docx (playbook, 4 pages)

If that looks good I’ll schedule the deep-dive and loop in our contracts lead.

Thanks — Jordan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
